candidates.topic: The Blue Hole of Dahab — Divers' Graveyard
candidates.teaser: There's a hole in the Red Sea that has swallowed over 200 divers — and nobody fully understands why it keeps pulling them in.
candidates.video_title: The Underwater Hole That Kills Expert Divers
candidates.video_description: The Blue Hole in Dahab, Egypt is one of the most beautiful dive sites on Earth — and one of the deadliest. Over 200 divers have died here, many of them highly experienced. A hidden arch at 56 meters depth triggers nitrogen narcosis before divers even realize what's happening.
candidates.script: Over 200 divers have died in this one single spot — and most of them were experts. The Blue Hole in Dahab, Egypt looks stunning from above, a perfect circle of electric blue water. But at exactly 56 meters down, there's a hidden arch. Divers aim for it. Nitrogen narcosis hits like silent drunk — your brain stops working before you notice. Many never come back up. Locals call it the Diver's Cemetery. Would you still jump in?

candidates.topic: The Rubber Hand Illusion — Brain Ownership Hack
candidates.teaser: Scientists tricked people into feeling pain in a rubber hand — and it reveals something unsettling about how your brain decides what is 'you.'
candidates.video_title: Your Brain Can Be Fooled Into Owning a Fake Hand
candidates.video_description: The Rubber Hand Illusion, first demonstrated in 1998, shows that the brain can adopt a fake limb as its own body within minutes. When the rubber hand is stabbed, participants physically flinch and their real hand's temperature drops. It reveals that body ownership is entirely constructed by the brain — not fixed reality.
candidates.script: Scientists put a rubber hand on a table, hid your real hand, then stroked both at the same time — and within 90 seconds, your brain adopted the fake one as yours. When they stabbed the rubber hand with a needle, participants screamed and their real hand's skin temperature dropped by one full degree. Your brain doesn't know what your body is — it just guesses, using whatever senses agree. So what exactly are you living inside?

candidates.topic: The Last Known Speaker — Language Death
candidates.teaser: In 2022, the last person on Earth who could speak a 500-year-old language died — and with her, an entire way of thinking about the world vanished forever.
candidates.video_title: A Language Died the Moment This Woman Did
candidates.video_description: When Cristina Calderón died in February 2022, the Yaghan language — spoken in Tierra del Fuego for over 500 years — went completely silent. Linguists say losing a language isn't just losing words; it's losing unique concepts, metaphors, and ways of perceiving reality that no other language ever captured.
candidates.script: When Cristina Calderón died in 2022, an entire language died with her. Yaghan — spoken at the southern tip of South America for over 500 years — had exactly one native speaker left: her. Linguists had raced to record every word. But Yaghan contained concepts no other language has — feelings and observations about the world that now simply have no name. When the last speaker of a language dies, what else disappears?

candidates.topic: Fasting Astronauts — Bone Loss in Space
candidates.teaser: Astronauts returning from six months in space have bones that aged 10 years — and the damage starts happening on day one.
candidates.video_title: Six Months in Space Ages Your Bones by a Decade
candidates.video_description: In microgravity, the human skeleton begins losing density almost immediately because bones exist to resist gravity — and without it, the body treats them as unnecessary. After six months aboard the ISS, astronauts lose up to 2% of bone density per month, equivalent to a decade of aging. Some damage never fully reverses.
candidates.script: The moment an astronaut reaches orbit, their skeleton starts dissolving. Without gravity pushing against your bones, your body decides they're no longer necessary. After just six months on the International Space Station, astronauts lose up to 12% of their total bone density — equivalent to aging ten years in one mission. Some never fully recover even after years back on Earth. The human body was never designed to leave this planet.

candidates.topic: The Voomerang Boomerang Effect — Stars Eating Their Own Planets
candidates.teaser: Astronomers just found a star that ate its own planets — and our Sun is scheduled to do the exact same thing to Earth.
candidates.video_title: Our Sun Will Swallow Earth — We Found Proof
candidates.video_description: In 2023, astronomers at MIT observed a star in real time consuming one of its own planets — the first direct observation of planetary engulfment ever recorded. The star, located 12,000 light-years away, brightened by a factor of 100 over ten days as it absorbed the planet. Our Sun is predicted to do the same to Mercury, Venus, and Earth in approximately 5 billion years.
candidates.script: In 2023, MIT astronomers watched a star eat a planet alive for the very first time in human history. The star, 12,000 light-years away, suddenly became 100 times brighter over ten days as it swallowed a world roughly the size of Jupiter. This wasn't a theory anymore — it was recorded, confirmed, published. And our own Sun is predicted to do the exact same thing to Earth in 5 billion years. The question is: will anything still be living here when it starts?
